ruling_pointer: .builder_queue/RULING_gh12_gate_determinism.md (option 3: deterministic leg in the arc, live draft as non-blocking smoke) and .builder_queue/RULING_arc_determinism_standing.md (a green that depends on uncontrolled inputs is not evidence; live-LLM legs run as non-blocking smoke and never gate)
options_cheapest_first: 1. Apply the ruled split to this leg: keep the deterministic half gating, move the single live-model draft into a non-blocking smoke leg (a test carrying @pytest.mark.live_smoke, which tools/arc_lega.sh already deselects via -m "not live_smoke"). tests/test_gh12_autoatlas.py already carries that marker, so the mechanism exists and is in use.

2. Leave the leg gating but make its failure non-silent and self-describing: catch the socket timeout and fail with a NAMED reason (LIVE_DRAFT_UNAVAILABLE) so a reader can tell a live-model red from a code red. Cheaper, but the arc's verdict still depends on GPU state.
3. Do nothing and keep reading leg A's verdict with this caveat in mind (status quo; rejected - it is how a real regression gets dismissed as 'the ollama flake').
not_proven: that GPU saturation was the ONLY cause of the 2026-09-13 19:4x red (it is the best-supported cause: four same-leg greens within the hour, same code, and the timeout is the client's 120 s, not an assertion); and whether the draft would have timed out with a longer client timeout rather than being genuinely stuck.
